brief.headline: Tech momentum dominates a neutral tape; gold and energy lose ground
brief.regime_summary: SPY sits 1.1% above its 50DMA and 7.6% above its 200DMA, with a 1-year drawdown of only 1.1%. That is constructive on the surface, but breadth is thin: only 4 of 11 sectors trade above their 50DMA. VIX at 16.32 is modestly above its 20DMA of 15.70, suggesting muted but edging anxiety. Sector momentum tells the same story: XLK leads at +8.6% over 20 days while eight sectors are negative, including Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Utilities and Real Estate all down 6-7%. This is a narrow, tech-driven rally. Headlines referenced treasury yields at 19-year highs and an intraday risk-off shift on September 23. Breakouts in this tape carry higher fade risk outside the leading sector.

portfolio.note: Price at $500.59 is only 0.2% above the 20DMA, RSI 56.3 and 20-day momentum +1.8%, so the stock is consolidating after a strong 40-day move (+27.5%). Earnings on October 28 are the next catalyst; RS vs the sector is -6.8%, so it is lagging within XLK.

Up 9.6% last week to $1,744.61, now 3.4% above the 20DMA with earnings on October 14. Trailing P/E of 59.9x is 52% above its historical median, and vol_20 of 41% means one ATR move equals about 5.4%. An ASML executive also warned publicly this week that Europe risks falling behind in chip investment, a watch item for forward guidance.

Down 2.0% last week to $62.37, now 2.1% below the 20DMA with RSI at 47.5 and 5.2% from the 20-day high. WTI fell 7.9% on the week and relative volume is elevated at 1.14, signalling active selling. The long-term DMA stack is still bullish but near-term momentum has stalled; cost basis is $88.00 and the position is down 29%.

GLD at $392.88 is below both the 20DMA ($402.28) and 40DMA ($400.23), 20-day momentum is -8.2%, and it sits 7.6% from its 20-day high. Gold futures also show -7.9% 20-day momentum and RSI at 39.4. The long-term MA stack is still bullish, but the thesis of near-term safe-haven support has weakened with the narrow tech rally drawing flows.

watchlist.name: CrowdStrike Holdings
watchlist.thesis: CRWD gained 8.3% last week and trades at $262.49, just 0.3% from its 20-day high of $263.19. 20-day RS vs the market is +37.2% and vs sector +29.0%. 47 analyst EPS revisions up vs 1 down over 30 days supports the move, and revenue growth estimate is 24.8% for the current year. The cybersecurity policy tailwind in headlines adds a near-term catalyst.
watchlist.risk: Forward P/E of 163x leaves no room for a miss; a single guidance cut would reverse a significant portion of the 40% 20-day move.

watchlist.name: Intel Corporation
watchlist.thesis: INTC is up 21.3% in one week to $122.60, now 21.3% above its 20DMA of $101.04 and 24.7% above its 40DMA. RSI is 70.3. CY EPS growth estimate is 261.9% and forward P/E is 59.5x. News flow this week included a Motley Fool piece predicting a major outside foundry customer named before 2027. Earnings are October 22.
watchlist.risk: A Simply Wall St. piece dated today notes the stock looks fully priced after a 293% run; the DMA stack is mixed, not full bull, and any foundry customer disappointment before October 22 could unwind quickly.

watchlist.name: Advanced Micro Devices
watchlist.thesis: AMD up 19.9% last week to $614.61, 19.8% above its 20DMA, RSI 71.0 and 20-day RS vs market +27.8%. EPS growth estimate for the current year is 81.7%. The stock is 1.6% from its 20-day high, suggesting the move is fresh rather than extended.
watchlist.risk: Trailing P/E of 154x is 52.8% above historical median; any macro risk-off repricing would hit the highest-multiple names first.

watchlist.name: Palantir Technologies
watchlist.thesis: PLTR at $191.79 is 8.1% above its 20DMA with 40-day momentum of +55.3% and relative volume at 1.26. P/E vs history is actually -51.8% below median, unusual for a high-growth name, and small positive EPS revisions (+0.26%) support the setup. Earnings November 2.
watchlist.risk: Trailing P/E is still 163.9x on reported earnings; if the broader market shifts risk-off on rate concerns, high-beta software names like PLTR typically compress fastest.

watchlist.name: Novo Nordisk
watchlist.thesis: NVO fell 8.5% last week to $38.17, now 20.6% below its 20-day high and 13.1% below its 20DMA. RSI is 27.7, bearish MA stack confirmed. EPS revisions are -2.1% and CY revenue growth estimate is -2.9%. Strategy Day this week failed to arrest the slide despite discussion of a direct NYSE listing and a positive oral Wegovy signal. P/E vs history is 2.37x the median.
watchlist.risk: RSI at 27.7 is deeply oversold; a confirmed oral Wegovy or pipeline catalyst could trigger a sharp technical bounce before the November 4 earnings.

watchlist.name: Comcast Corporation
watchlist.thesis: CMCSA down 5.0% last week to $22.55, RSI 30.8, 10.1% below its 20DMA and 17.3% from its 20-day high. CY EPS growth estimate is -18.8% with small negative EPS and revenue revisions. Relative volume is 1.36, suggesting active distribution. Earnings October 22.
watchlist.risk: Trailing P/E of 7.2x is cheap; a beat-and-raise on October 22 or any M&A headline could spark a violent short squeeze given the oversold RSI.

commodities.name: WTI Crude
commodities.note: Down 7.9% on the week to $93.85 despite a bullish longer-term MA stack; sits 12.1% from its 20-day high and just 1.0% below the 20DMA. RSI 51.4 is neutral. Watch whether XLE relative volume (1.14) signals further equity-side selling pressure.

commodities.name: Brent Crude
commodities.note: Holding better than WTI at $105.56, up 0.7% on the week and 5.6% above its 20DMA with RSI 61.7. The WTI/Brent spread widening is worth monitoring; thin liquidity flag means the move can be noisy.

commodities.name: Natural Gas
commodities.note: Up 10.1% last week to $3.193, at its 20-day high with RSI 69.1 and 20-day momentum +12.4%. Extremely thin relative volume (0.09) means the move should be treated cautiously; any seasonal demand confirmation would be the signal to watch.

commodities.name: Gold (Futures)
commodities.note: At $4,285.50, down 2.6% on the week and 3.1% below the 20DMA with RSI 39.4 and 20-day momentum -7.9%. The longer-term MA stack is still bullish but momentum is pointing lower; watch for a stabilization above the 100DMA before treating this as a pullback rather than a trend change.

commodities.name: Copper
commodities.note: Up 2.5% on the week to $6.7485, 2.6% above its 20DMA with RSI 58.7 and elevated relative volume at 2.6. Copper's positive posture contrasts with gold's weakness and suggests residual cyclical demand, though thin liquidity is flagged.

risks: Treasury yields referenced at 19-year highs mid-week; a further move higher would reprice multiples across the high-P/E tech leaders (INTC fwd 59x, CRWD fwd 163x, AMD 154x trailing) that are currently driving the market.
Breadth is dangerously narrow: only 4 of 11 sectors above their 50DMA. A rotation out of XLK would remove the entire engine of the current rally without a broad market to absorb it.

ASML earnings on October 14 and INTC earnings on October 22 arrive within three weeks. Both stocks have moved sharply; a miss by either would reverberate across the semiconductor complex including MSFT's AI infrastructure thesis.

GLD and XLE are both weakening simultaneously, which historically signals either a genuine risk-off rotation or dollar strength. The portfolio carries both; monitor the dollar index alongside these positions.

NVO's continued breakdown (RSI 27.6, -20.6% from 20-day high) after a high-profile Strategy Day suggests seller conviction, not just profit-taking. Healthcare sector 20-day momentum is -3.0%, and any NVO-specific pipeline negative would add pressure to the sector.
